headline: Sensex plunges over 1,100 points as surging crude oil prices and global yields trigger market crash

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Surging Brent crude oil prices put heavy pressure on Indian equities.
Higher US Treasury yields and weakness in global equity markets triggered sharp sell-offs.
BSE Sensex crashed over 1,100 points, dragging the Nifty50 index below 22,800.
Equity investors lost between Rs 6 lakh crore and Rs 8.92 lakh crore in market capitalization during the crash.
whatHappening: TRAI data showed Jio gained 2.4 million mobile users and Airtel gained 2.1 million users in August.
Ola Electric's board approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,000 crore with promoter participation.
Coforge named Akhil Gupta as Chairperson shortly after board exits.
The UAE signaled another $25 billion investment in India, targeting energy, ports, and space sectors.
summary:
Indian equities experienced a severe sell-off as the Sensex plunged over 1,100 points and Nifty dipped below 22,800 due to rising Brent crude and global yield pressures.
Despite market volatility, telecom giants Jio and Airtel posted solid subscriber additions for August according to TRAI data.
Corporate developments saw Ola Electric announce a Rs 1,000 crore rights issue while Coforge appointed Akhil Gupta as Chairperson.
